body:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: GPU OOMs detected on runner-43 during streaming decode. 125 error responses in last 3m, request drops observed. Auto-retry disabled. Paging oncall.

maria (oncall): I'm oncall, looking now. Any customer-facing symptoms?

sam (infra): We see container restarts + CUDA out-of-memory in k8s events. node-7 showing high GPU mem pressure. Attaching relevant logs.

devon (runtime): Logs show a long decode loop for several sessions — model kept generating past expected max_tokens. Suspect runaway generation from a requester.

alice (sre): Paging PD in case this escalates. Noted spike coincident with 18:22 UTC.

irina (cs): Customer reported streaming disconnects and 503s for several requests. Affected tenant: acme-corp, medium severity. They saw partial responses then drop.

maria (oncall): TL;DR: GPU OOM -> container crash -> request drops -> customer impact. Actions: (1) throttle new streaming requests to runner-43, (2) limit per-request decode tokens to 1024 at gateway, (3) restart runtime on runner-43, (4) trace affected request IDs for customer. Who can patch gateway throttling?

sam (infra): I can add a temporary iptables rate limit and update the LB to route new traffic away from node-7. Will cordon node-7.

/devon (runtime): I'll push a hotfix to reject requests with > max_tokens=2048 and to hard-fail if generation exceeds predicted token budget. Patch ready, want to roll to a single instance first.

maria (oncall): Good. Deploy plan: canary hotfix to runtime on runner-42, if stable, roll to runner-43 after cordon cleared. Keep customer notified.

deploy-bot: Starting canary deploy: runtime-image:v2-fix-decode-limit -> runner-42 (1/1). Logs streaming...

(devon pasted a code block):
```
# hotfix: enforce_server_max_tokens
if request.max_tokens > SERVER_MAX_TOKENS:
    reject(400, "max_tokens too large; server limit=1024")
# abort generation if token_count > request.max_tokens + safety_margin
```

alice (sre): Also enabling prefix/KV cache eviction for active sessions to free GPU mem on runner-43. Triggering cache prune now.

sam (infra): node-7 cordoned, LB drained. New streaming routed away. GPU mem on runner-43 dropping as containers get evicted.

maria (oncall): Any signs of recurring OOM after cache prune and routing change?

devon (runtime): Canary looks good so far on runner-42 (no OOMs in 2m). I'll approve rollout to other runners once deploy checks pass. I also added an abort path that cancels generation if the KV cache grows > threshold.

irina (cs): I told acme-corp support: we identified a runaway generation case causing request drops; we mitigated by routing traffic, restarting affected hosts, and applying a server hard-limit. They'll want a postmortem.

maria (oncall): Rolling runtime hotfix to runner-43 now after it drained. If it reappears, escalate to oncall lead.

deploy-bot: Rolling runtime-image:v2-fix-decode-limit -> runner-43 (1/1) completed.

sam (infra): Runner-43 restarted clean, GPU mem stable. No new OOM events for 5m. Node uncordoned.

devon (runtime): Confirmed logs: CUDA OOM stack (excerpt):
```
E CudaOOM: Out of memory when allocating 1.2G for attention_kv
  at runtime/decoder.cpp:482
  at serving/worker.cc:219
```
Root cause: single request triggered sustained decode sequence > configured client max_tokens; model config allowed extension; no server-side cap.

maria (oncall): Customer impact: acme-corp experienced ~12 failed streaming requests, intermittent 503s for 7m. No data exfiltration. Severity classified P2.

alice (sre): Follow-ups: (1) enforce server-side max_tokens=1024 in gateway + SDK clients, (2) add generation-length alert tied to GPU mem pressure, (3) add per-request GPU mem budgeting and pre-check before scheduling. I'll open tickets.

irina (cs): I'll coordinate a customer update and include mitigation steps and timeline.

maria (oncall): Action items captured. I'll start incident timeline + severity doc. If anyone has affected request IDs, drop them here.

devon (runtime): Adding request IDs: rq_9832, rq_9845, rq_9860 — these show continuous token generation for > 10k tokens.

alice (sre): Created follow-up tickets: INF-987 (server max_tokens guard), INF-988 (generation-length alert), INF-989 (per-request GPU budgeting). Assigning owners.

maria (oncall): Closing paging loop: system stable, customer notified, hotfix deployed. Moving to postmortem track. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident #2026 transitioned to RESOLVED by maria (oncall).
